Powerful permissions delegated on Organizational Units (OUs) in Active Directory can bypass standard security controls and pose a high risk if assigned inappropriately.

The indicator focuses on the following permissions:

  • Reanimate_Tombstone: Allows a user to restore deleted directory objects such as users or groups. This can be abused to bring back accounts that were intentionally removed, potentially with elevated privileges or outdated security settings.
  • Unexpire_Password: Enables a user to undo password expiration on other accounts. This may allow someone to reactivate dormant accounts or prevent password updates that are required for security policies.
  • SID_History: Grants the ability to modify the SIDHistory attribute of an account, which is used to impersonate or inherit permissions from another account. This is a common tactic in identity spoofing or lateral movement attacks.

While these permissions might be used for legitimate administrative tasks, their presence increases the risk of misuse or abuse, especially if assigned to non-administrative users.
